question.text: Tactical Asset Allocation involves making market calls to overweight or underweight certain asset classes. This approach is most suitable for:

answer.text: First-time investors who are new to financial markets
Conservative investors who prefer capital preservation
All investors regardless of their experience or surplus
Seasoned investors with large investible surpluses

explanation.text: The Logic: Tactical Asset Allocation involves overweighting or underweighting asset classes based on market calls. The workbook states that this approach is suitable only for seasoned investors with large investible surpluses. The Trap: Option C (all investors) is tempting for candidates who assume active management is universally beneficial. The workbook is explicit that the suitability of tactical calls is restricted to seasoned investors with large surpluses, not to first-time or conservative investors. Note: The workbook also advises that frequent tactical calls should be limited in size, so that the bulk of the portfolio continues to follow the strategic allocation.
